findings: An infiltrative pancreatic cancer measuring 19 mm is observed in the head of the pancreas. The common bile duct is interrupted by the tumor, suggesting invasion. There is contact of more than 180° with the portal vein, indicating potential invasion. No invasion beyond the inferior border of the duodenum is observed. No other local invasion factors are noted. Lymph node metastases are identified in two nodes at station 17 and four nodes at station 18. Multiple liver metastases are observed.

responses.content:
Task 1: Diagnose the local invasion factors of pancreatic cancer.

CH1 (Common bile duct invasion)
DU0 (No invasion beyond the inferior border of the duodenum)
S0 (No invasion of the superior mesenteric vein or artery)
RP0 (No invasion of the retroperitoneal tissues)
PV1 (Contact of more than 180° with the portal vein)
A0 (No invasion of the abdominal aorta)
PL0 (No invasion of the pancreatic lymphatic vessels)
OO0 (No invasion of the omentum)

Task 2: Determine the classification for local invasion (T classification) of pancreatic cancer.

Based on the image findings, the tumor is 19 mm in size and has contact of more than 180° with the portal vein, indicating potential invasion. The T classification is T3.

Task 3: Determine the N classification of pancreatic cancer.

Regional lymph nodes for pancreatic cancer are defined as follows:
- Head: stations 12, 13, 14, 15, 16
- Body: stations 8, 17, 18
- Tail: stations 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7

The patient's metastatic lymph node stations are 17 and 18, which are regional for the body of the pancreas. Counting only the metastatic lymph nodes within the regional stations, there are 6 metastatic lymph nodes (2 at station 17 and 4 at station 18). The N classification is N1b.

Task 4: Determine the M classification of pancreatic cancer.

Multiple liver metastases are observed, indicating distant metastasis. The M classification is M1.

Task 5: Determine the resectability classification of pancreatic cancer.

Based on the results of Task 1 and Task 4, the tumor has invaded the common bile duct and has contact of more than 180° with the portal vein, indicating potential invasion. However, regional lymph node involvement does not qualify as distant or non-regional metastasis. The resectability classification is Borderline Resectable (BR).

Task 6: Determine the overall stage according to the JPS staging system.

Based on the determined T (T3), N (N1b), and M (M1) categories, the overall stage is Stage IV.
